cases.learnTitle: Invasive carcinoma on breast ultrasound (proven by biopsy; radiologist outline)
cases.contextSource: Patient age from the dataset's clinical data.
cases.referenceSummary: The lesion is outlined freehand by a radiologist experienced in breast ultrasound, who also recorded its BI-RADS descriptors (Breast-Lesions-USG): shape irregular, margin not circumscribed (spiculated, indistinct), echo pattern hypoechoic, posterior features shadowing, BI-RADS 5. Diagnosis proven by biopsy. The image is the dataset's cropped B-mode frame with its true pixel size; no Doppler, no orientation.
cases.learnNotes: Breast ultrasound first answers one question: cyst or solid? A simple cyst is anechoic (black, no internal echoes), circumscribed with a thin sharp back wall, and has posterior acoustic enhancement (brighter tissue behind it, because fluid lets the sound through). Anything that fails these criteria is treated as solid or complicated. A solid mass is described like a mammographic one: shape (oval, round, irregular), orientation, margin (circumscribed or not: indistinct, angular, microlobulated, spiculated), echo pattern and posterior features. An oval, circumscribed mass parallel to the skin favors a benign tumor such as a fibroadenoma; an irregular, spiculated or angular hypoechoic mass with posterior shadowing is suspicious for carcinoma. Ultrasound shows the features; the biopsy gives the diagnosis.

cases.learnTitle: Fetal head on the standard plane for head circumference (sonographer's ellipse)
cases.referenceSummary: The ellipse on the outer skull was placed by a trained sonographer (HC18); the head circumference it gives is 87.3 mm. The image carries its true pixel size. Gestational age is not given by the dataset.
cases.learnNotes: Fetal growth is followed with standard measurements on standard planes. The head is measured on an axial plane through the thalami and the cavum septi pellucidi, with the skull outline symmetric and smooth. Bone reflects most of the sound, so the skull is a bright (echogenic) oval; the brain inside is darker. Head circumference is the perimeter of an ellipse placed on the outer edge of the skull: approximately pi x (BPD + OFD) / 2, where BPD (biparietal diameter) and OFD (occipitofrontal diameter) are the short and long axes. Measurements on an ultrasound image are only true distances when the image carries its pixel size, as these images do.
